nodes.name: Theorem 1.9
nodes.statement:
Fix $A > 2$, and let $\nu$ be a probability measure supported on $[0,1]^2$ satisfying (1.2). Let $n_1, n_2, \ldots$ be a lacunary sequence of positive integers, and let $\psi: \mathbb N \to [0,1]$.
		Then,
		\[
		\nu(\mathcal R(\psi)) = 1.
		\]

nodes.name: Theorem 1.4
nodes.statement:
Let $n_1, n_2, \ldots$ be a lacunary sequence of positive integers,
		let $A > 2$ be sufficiently large, and let $\nu$ be a probability measure supported on $[0,1]^2$ such that
		\begin{equation}
			
			\widehat \nu({\boldsymbol{\xi}}) \ll_A 
			(\log \| {\boldsymbol{\xi}} \|_\infty)^{-A}
			\qquad 
			(\|{\boldsymbol{\xi}} \|_\infty \to \infty).
		\end{equation}
		Let 
		$\psi: \mathbb N \to [0,1]$, and write
		$\mathcal W(\psi)$ for the set of 
		$({\beta},{\delta}) \in [0,1]^2$ such that
		\begin{equation}
			
			\| n_t {\beta} - {\delta} \| \leqslant \psi(t)
		\end{equation}
		has infinitely many solutions $t \in \mathbb N$. Then
		\[
		\nu(\mathcal W(\psi)) =
		\begin{cases}
			0, &\text{if } \displaystyle
			\sum_{t=1}^\infty
			\psi(t) < \infty \\ \\
			1, &\text{if } \displaystyle
			\sum_{t=1}^\infty
			\psi(t) = \infty.
		\end{cases}
		\]

nodes.name: Theorem 1.8
nodes.statement:
Let $n_1, n_2, \ldots$ be a lacunary sequence of positive integers, and let $\psi: \mathbb N \to [0,1]$. 
		
		
		
		Then, $\mathrm{dim}_{\mathrm{H}}
		(\mathcal R(\psi) \cap \mathcal B)
		= 2$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.6
nodes.statement:
Let $n_1, n_2, \ldots$ be a lacunary sequence of positive integers,
		and let $\psi: \mathbb N \to [0,1]$ with
		\[
		\sum_{t=1}^\infty \psi(t) = \infty.
		\]
		Then there exists $\mathcal G \subseteq \mathcal B$ with $\mathrm{dim}_{\mathrm{H}}(\mathcal G) = 2$ such that if $({\beta}, {\delta}) \in \mathcal G$ then the inequality
		(1.3) has infinitely many solutions $t \in \mathbb N$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement:
There exists $\eta > 0$ such that if
		$s \in (0,2)$ then there exists a probability measure $\nu$ supported on $\mathcal B$ with the following two properties:
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item  (Large Frostman dimension) 
			For any ball $I$ of radius 
			$r(I)$, we have
			\begin{equation}
				
				\nu(I) \ll_s r(I)^s.
			\end{equation}
			\item  (Polynomial Fourier decay)
			For any ${\boldsymbol{\xi}} \in \mathbb Z^2$, 
			we have
			\[
			\widehat \nu({\boldsymbol{\xi}}) \ll_\eta
			(1 + \| {\boldsymbol{\xi}} \|_\infty)^{-\eta}.
			\]
		\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Theorem 1.15
nodes.statement:
Fix $A > 2$, and let $\nu$ be a probability measure supported on $[0,1]^2$ satisfying (1.2). Let ${\alpha} \in \mathcal K$ and ${\gamma} \in \mathbb R$. Then
		\[
		\nu(\mathcal R(\alpha,\gamma))
		= 1.
		\]

nodes.name: Theorem 1.14
nodes.statement:
Let ${\alpha} \in \mathcal K$ and ${\gamma} \in \mathbb R$. Then
		\[
		\mathrm{dim}_H\mathcal R(\alpha,\gamma)
		=2.
		\]

nodes.name: Theorem 1.13
nodes.statement:
Let ${\alpha} \in \mathcal K$ and ${\gamma} \in \mathbb R$. Then there exists $\mathcal G \subseteq \mathcal B$ with $\mathrm{dim}_{\mathrm{H}}(\mathcal G) = 2$ such that if $({\beta}, {\delta}) \in \mathcal G$ then
		(1.8)
		holds.
